investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-06T13:27–13:34Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster has 0 of 6 nodes available to schedule a new kata peer-pod VM, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes failing pod node-affinity/selector matching. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent never reached a ready state and the eval runner collected zero evidence, violating all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler in the production-api environment cannot place the remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the affinity/selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the eligible nodes. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the pod never starts, so the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885, createAgent call) never receives a VM ID or remote state, leaving all required evidence fields empty.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector are occupied by existing peer-pod workloads, leaving no capacity for a new remote agent pod.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning the schedulable pool is already constrained to only 2 nodes. If those labels changed or nodes were cordoned/drained, the effective capacity shrinks further.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning or missing scale-out: the production cluster has only 6 nodes total with at most 2 eligible for kata peer-pod workloads; if the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node is low and no autoscaler is configured to add eligible nodes, any burst of remote agent creation will exhaust capacity.

QUATERNARY — Leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource: if prior eval runs or user sessions did not clean up their VMs, the resource slots remain consumed even when the workload is idle.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-06T13:27–13:34Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster has 0 of 6 nodes available to schedule a new kata peer-pod VM, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes failing pod node-affinity/selector matching. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent never reached a ready state and the eval runner collected zero evidence, violating all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler in the production-api environment cannot place the remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the affinity/selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the eligible nodes. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the pod never starts, so the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885, createAgent call) never receives a VM ID or remote state, leaving all required evidence fields empty.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 2 of 6 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the stage where it could collect evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message), causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted by the eval runner was stuck Unschedulable for ~135–148 seconds before the check timed out. No agent was ever created, so no runtime response was produced and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or its contracts.
